relevance_note: The paper reports 'a Japanese family containing two cases of autoinflammatory disease which exhibit an identical novel TNFAIP3 mutation' (proband and younger sister).
method_note: Read the whole paper (a short letter with no tables; Additional file 1/Table S1 with laboratory data is not in the Markdown, so lab values beyond those in the text are not reported). Built the JSON with a small Python script in my scratch directory; every value was typed from my own reading and every span was checked by script to occur verbatim in the paper. Individuals: the proband (called 'The patient' in the text and 'the proband (patient)' in Fig. 1), his younger sister (same variant), his mother (clinical features, deceased, not genotyped, so no variant row) and the unaffected father (Sanger-tested, no TNFAIP3 variant, so no variant row and no phenotype rows). The 'younger brothers of the proband without symptoms' were not sequenced and their number is not stated, so no rows were created for them. The sister is only said to have 'similar symptoms', so she has no phenotypic_features rows and all checklist items are 'not reported'. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) cDNA notation differs: text 'C596_598 del A' vs Fig. 1 legend 'c597-598 T deletion'; the text form was recorded in variant_original_string and cdna_hgvs_as_stated. (2) The variant is called a frameshift several times ('introduces a frameshift substitution', 'Cys200Alafsx16') but the discussion calls it 'a novel heterozygous missense mutation'; recorded as frameshift. (3) The Fig. 1 legend locates the variant 'in exon 4' (no exon field in the schema). Inheritance recorded as 'not reported': the father tested negative and the authors only state this is 'suggesting that these mutations were maternally derived'; the mother (deceased) was not reported as tested. Age: the proband was a '17-year-old' at referral with a 3-year history (onset 'at 14 years old'), and was admitted again 'Three years later' with no age given, so age at last evaluation is 'not reported'. 'Neither genital ulcer nor uveitis was confirmed' was treated as explicit absence for this individual; under the narrow/broad rule the checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' stays 'not reported'. 'There were no abnormalities except elevated levels of CRP' (laboratory data) was not used to exclude cytopenia or other checklist items because they are not named. Functional evidence (immunoblot) was done on the proband's PBMCs; it is repeated on the sister's variant row with that caveat. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null: the paper makes no statement either way.
